findings.source_passage: the insufferable splendors of God's throne. Well that Ahab's quadrant was furnished with coloured glasses, through which to take sight of that solar fire.
findings.why_it_matters: The transitional sentence 'Well that Ahab's quadrant was furnished with coloured glasses' is rhetorically distinctive — a dry, ironic aside that bridges cosmic description to physical action and is characteristic of Melville's narrator voice. The draft jumps straight to the action, losing the voice inflection.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Well that Ahab's quadrant was furnished with coloured glasses, through which to take sight of that solar fire' between the God's-throne image and the observation scene.

findings.source_passage: his wild face was subdued to an earthly passionlessness
findings.source_locator: paragraph 2, describing the Parsee during the observation
findings.why_it_matters: 'Subdued to an earthly passionlessness' is a sharply distinctive phrase carrying interpretive weight about the Parsee's inhuman nature; the draft replaces it with the neutral 'lids half-hooding his orbs' and drops the passionlessness entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'his wild face was subdued to an earthly passionlessness' after the description of the Parsee's half-hooded lids.

findings.source_passage: These eyes of mine look into the very eye that is even now beholding him; aye, and into the eye that is even now equally beholding the objects on the unknown, thither side of thee, thou sun!
findings.why_it_matters: The draft cuts the crucial second clause — 'aye, and into the eye that is even now equally beholding the objects on the unknown, thither side of thee, thou sun!' — which is interpretively essential: it is Ahab's leap from tracking Moby Dick to a metaphysical claim about omniscience and the far side of the sun. Truncating it to a plain statement about Moby Dick flattens the passage's visionary character.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'These eyes of mine look into the very eye that is even now beholding him; aye, and into the eye that is even now equally beholding the objects on the unknown, thither side of thee, thou sun!'

findings.source_passage: As the frantic old man thus spoke and thus trampled with his live and dead feet
findings.why_it_matters: 'His live and dead feet' is a charged, characteristic Melvillean locution — the wooden leg motif rendered in a single compressed phrase. The draft omits the entire framing sentence, losing this motif marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce the Parsee's reaction with 'As the frantic old man thus spoke and thus trampled with his live and dead feet' to preserve the live/dead foot motif.

summary: The draft preserves most of the major set-pieces but drops three medium-severity voice/interpretive passages — the 'earthly passionlessness' characterisation of the Parsee, the truncation of Ahab's visionary sun-apostrophe, and the narrator's dry 'Well that Ahab's quadrant' transition — plus the 'live and dead feet' motif marker, triggering regeneration on the three-medium threshold.
